# Ezra Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 469r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EZR_003_page_001.jpg

---

**1** When the seventh month arrived and the Israelites had settled in their towns, the people came together with one purpose in Jerusalem.

**2** Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, together with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives, rebuilt the altar of the God of Israel so they could sacrifice burnt offerings on it, following what is written in the Law of Moses, the man of God.

**3** Even though they were afraid of the peoples already living in the land, they set the altar on its original site and began offering burnt offerings to the LORD — both the morning and evening sacrifices.

**4** They also celebrated the Festival of Shelters as prescribed, offering the required number of burnt offerings for each day, **5** and after that they presented the regular daily burnt offerings, the new moon sacrifices, and the offerings for all of the LORD's appointed festivals, as well as all the freewill offerings brought to the LORD.

**6** On the first day of the seventh month they began offering sacrifices to the LORD, even though the foundation of the LORD's temple had not yet been laid.

**7** They paid the stonecutters and carpenters, and they provided food, drink, and olive oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre in exchange for cedar logs from Lebanon, which were floated down by sea to Joppa. King Cyrus of Persia had authorized all of this.

**8** In the second month of the second year after arriving at God's temple in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, and the rest of their people — priests, Levites, and all who had returned from captivity — began the work. They put the Levites twenty years of age and older in charge of supervising the construction of the LORD's temple.

**9** Jeshua and his sons and relatives, Kadmiel and his sons (descendants of Hodaviah), and the sons of Henadad and their sons and relatives — all Levites — joined together to supervise the workers building God's temple.

**10** When the builders completed the foundation of the LORD's temple, the priests took their places in their ceremonial robes, holding trumpets, while the Levites from the family of Asaph stood with cymbals. Together they praised the LORD, following the pattern established by King David of Israel.

**11** They sang back and forth, praising and thanking the LORD: "He is good! His faithful love for Israel endures forever!" Then all the people burst into a tremendous shout of praise to the LORD because the foundation of his temple had been laid.

**12** But many of the older priests, Levites, and family leaders who remembered Solomon's temple began to weep loudly when they saw the new foundation. Others, however, shouted for joy. **13** The joyful shouting and the weeping were so mingled together that no one could tell the difference. The sound of the people carried far into the distance.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 3 — Worship in the face of fear:** The returnees rebuilt the altar first — before walls, before the temple, before any protection. Their first act in a hostile land was not to build defenses but to worship. The text suggests their fear actually drove them to the altar rather than away from it.

**Verses 11-13 — When joy and grief are the same sound:** This is one of the most emotionally powerful moments in the Old Testament. The older generation wept because they remembered the glory of Solomon's temple and knew this one would not compare. The younger generation shouted with joy because they had never known anything but exile. Both responses were genuine worship. The narrator's observation that no one could distinguish the two sounds may be the theological point: in God's hearing, the weeping and the joy were equally valid praise.

*— PNEUMA*
